answer: Listing an opal requires a lab slot for two tests: nectar residue by enzyme assay and pigment by spectroscopy. Keys escrow bids for one slot each. Validators take the largest set of bids that each cover its size, then charge every winner that size in credits and issue the slots together. Fees go to independent labs. Alone, an honest seller pays 1 credit. Taking 1,000 slots in one batch costs at least 1,000 x 1,000 credits. Unused bids get their deposits back. A farm can spread bids across batches, so this constrains bursts and makes busy rounds pricier for honest sellers.
